summary: Azelastine hydrochloride is a second-generation H1-antihistamine used topically as a nasal spray and as ophthalmic drops. The nasal spray is indicated for the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis (in adults and children 5 years and older) and for vasomotor rhinitis (in adults and adolescents 12 years and older); the ophthalmic form treats itching of allergic conjunctivitis. For seasonal allergic rhinitis the adult/adolescent dose is one or two sprays per nostril twice daily; the paediatric (5-11 years) dose is one spray per nostril twice daily; vasomotor rhinitis is treated with two sprays per nostril twice daily. Besides H1 antagonism it has mast cell stabilising and anti-inflammatory properties. Although applied topically, somnolence can occur, so patients should avoid hazardous activities requiring alertness and should avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants. A bitter taste is the most frequently reported effect of the nasal spray.
indications: Symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis in adults and pediatric patients 5 years and older (nasal spray)
Symptoms of vasomotor rhinitis in adults and adolescent patients 12 years and older (nasal spray)
Itching of the eye associated with allergic conjunctivitis (ophthalmic solution)

admin: For intranasal or ophthalmic topical use only - do not swallow
Prime the nasal spray before first use and when it has not been used for 3 or more days
Tilt the head slightly forward and breathe in gently while spraying to limit drainage into the throat (reduces bitter taste)
For the eye drops, do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface; remove contact lenses first
Avoid alcohol and other CNS depressants because of additive drowsiness
Do not drive or operate machinery until you know how it affects you
moa: Azelastine is a phthalazinone derivative and selective histamine H1-receptor antagonist. In addition to competitive H1 blockade, it stabilises mast cells, inhibiting the release of histamine and other mediators, and reduces the influx and activation of inflammatory cells and the synthesis of leukotrienes, kinins and other pro-inflammatory mediators. Applied topically to the nasal mucosa or conjunctiva, these combined antihistaminic, mast cell stabilising and anti-inflammatory actions relieve the itching, sneezing, rhinorrhoea and congestion of allergic and vasomotor rhinitis and the ocular itch of allergic conjunctivitis.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to azelastine or any component of the formulation
relative: Activities requiring full mental alertness (somnolence risk)
Concurrent alcohol or other CNS depressants
Pregnancy and lactation (use only if clearly needed)

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Animal studies at high systemic doses showed developmental toxicity. Because systemic exposure from intranasal/ophthalmic use is low, the clinical risk is expected to be small, but azelastine should be used during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether azelastine is excreted in human milk after topical administration. Given the low systemic exposure, the amount in milk is likely small; use caution when administering to a breastfeeding woman and consider monitoring the infant for drowsiness.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided for topical azelastine; systemic absorption is low. Use the usual recommended dose and monitor for systemic effects in significant impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is provided for topical azelastine; systemic absorption is low. Azelastine is hepatically metabolised (to the active metabolite desmethylazelastine), so use with general caution in significant impairment.

major: Other CNS depressants - sedatives, hypnotics, opioids (additive somnolence)
moderate: Cimetidine and ketoconazole increased plasma azelastine levels with oral dosing (less relevant for topical use)
minor: Other topical nasal/ocular products - separate administration
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive CNS depression and somnolence

rare: Nasal septum perforation / ulceration (with prolonged nasal use)

Nasal mucosa: epistaxis, irritation, ulceration with prolonged use
counsel: This is a nose spray (or eye drop) for allergy symptoms - use it as directed, usually twice a day
Prime a new nasal spray and re-prime it if you have not used it for a few days
Tilt your head forward and sniff gently to reduce the bitter taste running into your throat
It can make you sleepy even though it is a spray - avoid alcohol and do not drive until you know how it affects you
A bitter taste and mild nasal stinging or occasional nosebleeds can occur
For eye drops, do not touch the dropper to your eye and remove contact lenses first
pk: Symptom relief often within ~15-30 minutes of nasal dosing
Systemic Tmax about 2-3 hours after nasal administration
Azelastine ~22 hours; active metabolite desmethylazelastine ~50-90 hours
Supports twice-daily dosing; effect maintained over the dosing interval
Store upright at controlled room temperature (about 20-25 degrees C); do not freeze
pearls: Topical antihistamine, but somnolence can still occur - counsel against driving/hazardous tasks and avoid alcohol/CNS depressants.
Bitter taste is the most common complaint of the nasal spray; spraying with the head tilted forward and sniffing gently reduces it.
Fast onset (within ~15-30 min) makes it useful for rapid relief of allergic rhinitis symptoms, including congestion.
Prime the device before first use and after 3 or more days of non-use to ensure accurate dosing.
Different products/concentrations exist; check the specific dose for allergic versus vasomotor rhinitis.
Prolonged nasal use rarely causes septal irritation or ulceration - inspect the nasal mucosa if symptoms occur.
missed: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular twice-daily schedule - do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There have been no reported overdoses with the nasal spray, and acute overdose by an adult is unlikely to cause clinically significant effects other than increased somnolence (one bottle contains a limited amount of drug). General supportive measures should be used; there is no specific antidote. Oral ingestion of antihistamines can cause serious effects in young children, so keep the product out of their reach; manage accidental ingestion with supportive care.
